boundary_rationale: A third-person narrative frame opens the row: "וַיְהִ֡י בִּימֵ֣י אָ֠חָז בֶּן יוֹתָ֨ם בֶּן עֻזִּיָּ֜הוּ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֗ה עָלָ֣ה רְצִ֣ין מֶֽלֶךְ אֲ֠רָם וּפֶ֨קַח בֶּן רְמַלְיָ֤הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה עָלֶ֑יהָ וְלֹ֥א יָכֹ֖ל לְהִלָּחֵ֥ם עָלֶֽיהָ" (oshb:Isa.7.1, byte tier), matching “In the days of Ahaz the son of Jotham, the son of Uzziah, king of Judah, Rezin the king of Syria and Pekah the son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up to Jerusalem to war against it, but could not prevail against it.” (web:Isa.7.1) -- a clean scene shift from the throne-vision report. Four verse-initial speech onsets punctuate the span without reopening it: "וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָה֮ אֶֽל יְשַׁעְיָהוּ֒" (oshb:Isa.7.3, byte tier), matching “Then Yahweh said to Isaiah” (web:Isa.7.3); "כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה" (oshb:Isa.7.7, byte tier), matching “This is what the Lord Yahweh says” (web:Isa.7.7); "וַיּ֣וֹסֶף יְהוָ֔ה דַּבֵּ֥ר אֶל אָחָ֖ז לֵאמֹֽר" (oshb:Isa.7.10, byte tier), matching “Yahweh spoke again to Ahaz, saying,” (web:Isa.7.10); and "וַיֹּ֕אמֶר שִׁמְעוּ נָ֖א בֵּ֣ית דָּוִ֑ד" (oshb:Isa.7.13, byte tier), matching “Listen now, house of David” (web:Isa.7.13). These four stand inside the third-person narrative frame opened at web:Isa.7.1 rather than beside it, so the frame owns the embedded speech and nothing among the four reopens the row; the same narrative frame does not extend past its own close, which is why its defective-spelled resumptive twin at oshb:Isa.8.5 opens a fresh row rather than continuing this one. The frame runs through the Immanuel sign to its closing threat, “Yahweh will bring on you, on your people, and on your father’s house days that have not come, from the day that Ephraim departed from Judah, even the king of Assyria.” (web:Isa.7.17), where the next verse’s repeated “in that day” formula (web:Isa.7.18) opens a different oracle cycle. The seam is best argued not from the day-formula's own recurrence, which recurs across web:Isa.7.18-Isa.7.25 and which cannot discriminate the cut on its own, but from a frame-mode shift at MT 7:18 itself: the narrated direct-address scene that has framed the intervening speech since web:Isa.7.1 gives way here to an impersonal formulaic oracle cycle that names no speaker and addresses no one directly.

These four images bind the fly/bee, razor, and briers-and-thorns pictures into one oracle cycle addressed to the same audience as the preceding narrative but marked off from it by their own repeated formula rather than a fresh scene. The cycle runs to “All the hills that were cultivated with the hoe, you shall not come there for fear of briers and thorns; but it shall be for the sending out of oxen, and for sheep to tread on.” (web:Isa.7.25), where chapter 8’s sign-act command (web:Isa.8.1) opens a new divine-command frame.
